location.ref: Bāul songs on the Uncatchable Man and the tide (summary only)

paraphrase: The Uncatchable Man (adhar mānuṣ) is said in coded songs to come and go in the body with the tide at a certain time, like a fish swimming upstream; only the practitioner guided by the guru, going against the current (ujān), can catch him; the songs warn that the one who goes with the current is lost.
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D
notes: Skeleton from memory (Phase B). RESTRICTED: summary and warnings only. Coded content; outline from the ethnographic literature.

location.ref: Bāul teaching on bartamān and anumān

paraphrase: Bāuls call themselves followers of the present (bartamān): they accept what can be known in the living body here and now, and set aside inference and hearsay (anumān) — scripture, heaven, the gods of the books — as unverified.
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D
notes: Skeleton from memory (Phase B). Recurrent Bāul teaching (in songs and in teachers' explanations); not one song.

location.ref: Bāul songs on the 'four moons' (summary only)

paraphrase: The songs speak in code of 'four moons' (cāri candra) in the body that the practitioner must come to know under the guru; they warn that without a guru and without mastery of desire the practice leads to ruin and to falling into lust, and that it must be kept secret.
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D
notes: Skeleton from memory (Phase B). RESTRICTED: summary and the tradition's own warnings only; no method is recorded. Content from the ethnographic literature in outline.

location.ref: song of Gagan Harkarā 'āmi kothāy pāba tāre, āmār maner mānuṣ ye re …'

paraphrase: Where shall I find him, the Man of my Heart? Having lost him I wander in search of him from land to land.
speaker: Gagan Harkarā

original.text: āmi kothāya pāba tāre, āmāra manera mānuṣa ye re
original.edition: popular printed and sung form; wording varies between editions and singers

translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D

location.ref: Bāul maxim 'je āche bhāṇḍe, tā āche brahmāṇḍe'

paraphrase: What is in the vessel (the body) is in the universe: the whole cosmos, its gods, rivers and pilgrim places, is present in the human body, so the search is conducted in the body.
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D
notes: Skeleton from memory (Phase B). Proverbial maxim shared with Sahajiyā and Nāth usage (cf. 'yat piṇḍe tat brahmāṇḍe').

location.ref: song of Madan Bāul 'tomār path ḍhāikyāche mandire masjide …'

paraphrase: Your path, Lord, is covered over by temples and mosques; I hear your call but cannot move — guru and murśid stand in the way, blocking me.
speaker: Madan Bāul

original.edition: popular printed and sung form; wording varies between editions and singers
